text:
Zoe Park: hey folks — quick Q before my first day Monday. I paid a moving company based in Germany for my relocation and they invoiced in EUR. What’s the process to get reimbursed? Do you accept invoices in EUR, and is there a special relocation form? Also, vendor included VAT — should I send VAT info or do you need the net amount? One more thing: my start date overlaps the company-observed public holiday — will that change prorated PTO or benefits effective date?

Maya (People Ops): welcome Zoe! :tada: Yes we accept invoices in EUR. Steps: 1) Upload the original invoice + proof of payment to Expensify (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/x/Relocate) 2) Fill the "Relocation Reimbursement Form" (linked in the page) 3) If invoice != bank charge, include bank statement showing payment.

Maya (People Ops): VAT: we reimburse the gross amount you paid. We cannot reclaim EU VAT on behalf of employees, so if you are able to reclaim VAT personally, note that in the form. Please include the VAT line on the invoice so we can code it correctly.

Sam (Payroll): tagging in payroll details. If you’re a US employee we process the relocation reimbursement as a non-cash benefit per policy — typically paid on a separate payroll run and may be taxable depending on amount/type. If you’re on an international contract, we may route it through AP and pay via wire. We’ll need your W-9 or W-8BEN on file (depending on tax residency).

Sam (Payroll): timeline: submit complete docs and approvals -> expect reimbursement in ~1 payroll cycle (5–10 business days). For EUR invoices we convert to USD using the company FX snapshot dated on payment; include the invoice date and amount.

onboard-bot: :page_facing_up: Expense checklist template added to thread: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/x/Relocate#checklist — include: invoice, proof-of-payment, relocation form, exchange-rate note if non-USD.

Zoe Park: thanks! two follow-ups — (1) vendor charged me in EUR but refunded a small admin fee later, should I submit both invoices/credit note? (2) about the holiday — I start the day before the observed holiday, does that delay benefits effective date or PTO accrual?

Maya (People Ops): (1) yes include the credit note so we net the amounts correctly. Mark the credit note in the relocation form and attach matching bank entries. (2) Benefits: your benefits effective date is your official start date unless otherwise noted in your offer. Holiday: since the holiday is company-observed, it does not delay benefits. PTO accrual: prorated based on start date; because you start the day before a holiday the accrual window is the same — we’ll confirm the exact prorated days after payroll runs.

Sam (Payroll): Zoe — can you DM me the invoice total in USD (or the EUR amount + invoice date) and the last 4 of your bank account? I’ll pre-check tax treatment.

Zoe Park: sent DM with EUR amount (3,450.00) and last 4 digits. Also uploaded invoice + credit note to the Expensify page.

Maya (People Ops): got it, thanks. I’ll review and route for approval. Expect an email confirmation when routed to payroll. :slightly_smiling_face:

Zoe Park: amazing — really appreciate the quick help!
